subject: Order Form redline: liability, credits, and sole-remedy mechanics
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form redline: liability, credits, and sole-remedy mechanics

Team — moving Tempest towards signature next week. Attached is my suggested Order Form redline (OrderForm_Tempest_redline.docx) that I want to run by Legal before we send to the customer. Key points: 

- Limitation of liability: cap should be the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $1,500,000 floor.
- Consequential damages: standard carve-out (no liability for indirect/consequential).
- Service credits: Customer can claim credits for SLA breaches; credits operate as the exclusive monetary remedy for service availability/latency SLA breaches, with a 50% cap of monthly fees in the affected month.
- Sole remedy language: Order Form currently says "sole and exclusive remedy" — I want Legal to confirm this wording works with our indemnities and does not unintentionally bar relief for IP infringement or gross negligence.

Please review and flag any hard stops. If Legal wants to remove the $1.5M floor we need a commercial note (Karikth) on how that impacts pricing/coverage. I plan to present to Marcel/Emily next Tue unless we hear otherwise.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Order Form redline: liability, credits, and sole-remedy mechanics

Laura — thanks for the draft. High-level Legal feedback after initial pass: 

1) Sole remedy: we should avoid an absolute "sole remedy" formulation that could be read to bar statutory remedies or claims for IP infringement and gross negligence. Suggest: "exclusive monetary remedy for service-related claims, except for (i) indemnity claims, (ii) claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence, and (iii) claims for IP infringement or violations of law."

2) Liability cap: tying to 12 months' fees is standard; the $1.5M floor is company-exposure sensitive. For this enterprise buyer I can accept a $1.5M floor if Sales confirms that the expected ARR for year one justifies it. If not, propose removing the floor and keeping a straight 12-month fees cap.

3) Credit mechanics: earmarking credits as the primary monetary remedy is OK, but a flat 50% monthly-fee cap may be high from a legal exposure standpoint if combined with other carve-outs. We often negotiate a per-incident cap + annual aggregate cap. Example compromise: per-incident credit capped at 25% of the monthly fee, aggregate credits in a 12-month period capped at 50% of annual fees.

4) Remedies interplay: ensure "credits do not reduce customer's right to seek injunctive relief or to pursue claims under indemnities." Add explicit sentence.

I redlined the attached (OrderForm_Tempest_redline.docx) with suggested language. If Sales wants to keep the $1.5M floor, provide a short commercial justification (expected spend/criticality) and I'll escalate to Legal Ops for SLA playbook exception.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Order Form redline: liability, credits, and sole-remedy mechanics

Thanks Neha — appreciate the detailed read. Commercial context for Tempest (to justify the floor): 

- Expected first-year spend: ~$2.1M (committed + expected overage).
- Use case: customer will embed our hosted API in a revenue-generating analytics product; latency SLOs are material to their GTM.

From Sales perspective: 
- We need the $1.5M floor to keep total contract value protected for RD investments; dropping to pure 12-month fees (which would be ~ $2.1M anyway) might be OK, but having a floor gives predictability for other similar accounts.
- On credits: Tempest will push hard for uncapped credits. I can accept Neha's per-incident 25% + annual aggregate 50% compromise as a good balance. If Legal insists on per-incident 25% but no annual aggregate, the customer may push back.

Attachments: MAP_Tempest_v2.xlsx, pricing-sheet-tempest.pdf.

If Legal can sign off on Neha's suggested lockboxes (IP/indemnity carve-outs + per-incident/annual credit caps), I'm comfortable moving the redline to the customer. If we need $1.5M floor called out in the Order Form, I can defend it with the numbers above.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Sales

All — I reviewed the thread and Neha's redlines look reasonable. Next steps: 

1) Proceed with Neha's language that makes credits the exclusive monetary remedy for service claims while preserving carve-outs for indemnities, gross negligence, and IP.
2) Try to land on the compromise credit mechanics: per-incident credit cap 25% of monthly fees, annual aggregate credits capped at 50% of annual fees. If Tempest pushes, Karthik is authorized to go to 50% per-incident for the latency SLA only, subject to my sign-off if they demand the $1.5M floor be removed.
3) If Tempest counters and refuses the aggregate cap, escalate to CRO for approval of an exception. 

Karhik — send the updated Order Form redline to Marcel/Emily with a short cover note summarizing the change and the DocuSign preview link below. Let's aim for signature by EOD Thu.
